hero.title: Store what matters. Choose who inherits it. Let an impartial clock do the rest.
hero.subtitle: Cryple is a zero-knowledge digital inheritance protocol. Everything is encrypted on your device, and its release to your heirs is decided by a smart contract on Arbitrum — not by us, and not by anyone who could be persuaded, hacked, or shut down.
hero.demoTitle: The Dead Man's Switch, Running in Public
hero.demoSubtitle: The clock lives on a public blockchain. Nothing on our side can stop it, restart it, or check in on your behalf — only you can.
hero.demoStage1: Check-in signed on your device — clock reset
hero.demoStage2: No check-in past your inactivity period — contest window open
hero.demoStage3: Contest period elapsed — your heirs can open exactly what you left them

features.title: Why is Cryple Different?
features.subtitle: We are not a password manager, and you are not the product — no ads, no tracking, no cookies. Cryple does one thing: it makes sure the people you chose can open what you left them, and that nobody else ever can. Including us.

items.title: The Digital Legacy Protocol
items.desc: Your dead man's switch lives on Arbitrum. It counts your silence, opens a contest window, and authorizes release entirely on-chain. Anyone can advance a switch whose deadline has genuinely passed — an heir, a guardian, a public keeper bot — so the release is never ours to delay, deny, or quietly forget. What we do still hold is the encrypted data itself: the chain governs when your heirs may open it, not whether it is there to open.

items.title: You Are Not The Product
items.desc: No ads, no tracking, no cookies. Our free subscription is truly free, and you pay for more features if you like the product. Real Zero-Knowledge. The locks and keys to access your vault are created on your device. We cannot see your passwords, read your notes, or access your files under any circumstances.

items.title: Exactly Who Inherits Exactly What
items.desc: Name your heirs and assign specific items to each one. The key for every item is re-encrypted for that person alone, on your device, while you are alive. Heirs are never notified — telling someone they were named would publish a relationship you may have chosen to keep private.

items.title: Silence Is Not Death, So You Always Get to Object
items.desc: A missed check-in releases nothing. It opens a contest period that is visible to you and cancellable by you: one signed “I'm alive” returns the switch to normal. You set both durations — how long silence lasts before your heirs can act, and how long you then have to stop it.

items.title: Guardians Get You Back In Without Getting In
items.desc: Your recovery key is split so that any k of n pieces rebuild it and anything fewer reveals nothing at all — not a partial answer, not a head start. Guardians are invited and must accept, you always hold one piece yourself as a printed Recovery Kit, and every piece is encrypted for its guardian alone. They cannot read each other's, and we cannot read any.

items.title: Your Recovery Phrase Is the Account
items.desc: Twelve or twenty-four ordinary words, generated in your browser. Every key Cryple uses is derived from them the same way on every device — including the signer of your on-chain account. No email, no password reset, no wallet extension, no gas fees. Type the phrase into a new browser and your vault is simply there.

items.title: Paranoid Mode - 6 digit PIN as 2FA
items.desc: Both modes use a 6-digit PIN to lock the app and encrypt the copy of your phrase on that device. In Standard mode it stays local — forget it and you simply sign back in with your phrase. In Paranoid mode the server checks it too, so it becomes a true second factor: a stolen phrase alone gets nobody in, and a forgotten PIN is reset through your guardians.

items.title: Built to Outlive Its Own Algorithms
items.desc: Inheritance runs on a timescale of decades, and data captured today can be stored and attacked later. Your own vault is sealed with symmetric encryption keyed from your phrase — the kind a quantum computer does not break. The one place that is not enough is encrypting for another person, where two people who share no secret must agree on a key: exactly what quantum computers are expected to break. So a guardian's share and an heir's item key are wrapped with two independent algorithms at once, one classical and one post-quantum. An attacker has to break both. If either survives, your data stays sealed.

howItWorks.title: How It Works? (Four Steps, Then You're Done)
howItWorks.subtitle: You set it up once, while you can still make the decisions. After that, all it ever asks of you is a check-in.

steps.title: 1. Generate Your Recovery Phrase
steps.desc: Open Cryple and your browser generates twelve or twenty-four words, then derives your whole key tree from them locally. Nothing is sent anywhere. Write the phrase down on paper, and choose Standard or Paranoid mode.

steps.title: 2. Fill the Vault
steps.desc: Store the small things that unlock everything else — seed phrases, account details, credentials. Write notes: the letters and instructions that explain them. Write long-form documents that sync across your devices. All of it encrypted here, before it leaves.

steps.title: 3. Name Guardians and Heirs
steps.desc: Invite guardians who can help you back in if you lose your phrase, then name your heirs and give each one exactly the items they should receive. Everything is re-encrypted for them on your device, while you are alive.

steps.title: 4. Check In, and Live Your Life
steps.desc: One signed check-in resets the clock. Keep checking in and nothing ever happens. Stop, and the contest window opens — visible to you, cancellable by you — and only after it expires can your heirs open what you left them.

security.title: Security You Can Verify
security.subtitle: Zero-knowledge by construction, not by policy: the server never receives anything readable, and the release is decided by a public contract instead of by us.
bullets: Everything is encrypted in your browser; the server receives sealed data and stores it
Zero-knowledge by construction — there is no key on our side to decrypt with
Proof of ownership by ECDSA P-256 signature over a fresh challenge, never a transmitted secret
Post-quantum key wrapping with ML-KEM-768 (Kyber) for every heir and guardian
Hybrid PQXDH: X25519 + ML-KEM-768 combined, so classical and quantum attacks must both succeed
Paranoid Mode: a real second factor, requiring your seed phrase and your PIN together
Your recovery phrase, your PIN and your plaintext never leave your device, ever
The dead man's switch is a contract on Arbitrum — nothing server-side can check in on your behalf

sections.title: 1. Zero-Knowledge Architecture
sections.content: Cryple is built from the ground up as a zero-knowledge service. Our mathematical models guarantee that no employee, administrator, or attacker compromising our servers can read your stored legacy items, credentials, or notes.
sections.note: We operate strictly under the following policy:
items: Your recovery phrase and your PIN never leave your browser.
All encryption/decryption happens locally on your device before transmission.
We only store randomly generated salts, ECDSA public keys, and encrypted payloads.

sections.title: 2. Cryptography Practices
sections.content: We leverage industry-standard cryptographic tools:
items: Authentication: ECDSA P-256 signatures over a client-generated challenge; in Paranoid Mode the PIN is stretched client-side with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) and stored server-side as an Argon2id hash.
Signing: Asymmetric public/private key-pairs (ECDSA P-256) are derived client-side from your recovery phrase and sign every challenge and privileged action.
Data Storage: Legacy items, notes and documents are encrypted on the client device using AES-256-GCM.
Post-Quantum: Anything encrypted for another person — a guardian's share, an heir's item key — is wrapped with the hybrid PQXDH construction, X25519 combined with ML-KEM-768.

sections.title: 3. Infrastructure Protection
sections.content: Our server infrastructure is protected by rigorous engineering limits against attack vectors:
items: Rate limiting is enforced heavily across all API ingress nodes to prevent bruteforcing.
We use atomic single-use nonce locking to prevent Replay Attacks for all sensitive authentication flows.
Database volumes and object storage buckets are encrypted at rest via our cloud providers.
The inheritance clock is a smart contract on Arbitrum, not a server job: nothing on our side can check in on a user's behalf, and no outage of ours can stop it.

sections.title: 4. What This Model Does Not Cover
sections.content: A security policy that lists only strengths is marketing. These are the limits of our architecture, stated plainly, so you can weigh them before you rely on us.
sections.note: Each of these is a known and accepted limitation of the current design, not an oversight:
items: Data availability. Your encrypted data lives in our storage. The blockchain proves what that data was and decides when your heirs are authorized to open it, but it cannot serve the data itself. If our storage were lost or withheld, the on-chain proof would survive and the ciphertext would not. The chain removes our discretion over the timing of an inheritance; it does not remove our custody of the bytes.

The confidentiality window. An heir's wrapped key is stored from the moment you assign it, alongside the ciphertext. A compromised backend could hand both to an heir before the switch has fired, and that heir's own keys would open them. No contract can prevent this, because no contract ever holds key material. The chain guarantees the timing of authorization and the integrity of the data — not the confidentiality window.

Recipient key authenticity. The public keys of your guardians and heirs are served by our API. A malicious backend could substitute its own keys at setup time and read what was wrapped for that person afterwards. Out-of-band verification of key fingerprints is the mitigation, and it is not built yet.

sections.title: 5. Auditing & Open Source
sections.content: We believe security requires transparency. Therefore, our target is an "Open Source Client" philosophy, meaning all client-side decryption logic is inspectable by security researchers before usage.
sections.note: We are presently undergoing internal security reviews ahead of formal independent third-party penetration testing.

sections.title: 6. Vulnerability Disclosure
sections.content: If you discover a security issue or vulnerability please report it immediately rather than disclosing it publicly. We are working on a Bug Bounty program, but in the meantime please contact our security team.
